title: Transparent fallback timer and heartbeat surge mender (hotpatch)
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Fix: Add transient heartbeat smoothing and controlled fallback timer to reduce noisy regional failovers during short probe storms. No customer-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: We observed an increase in short heartbeat spikes (1-5s) from probe jitter and transient network blips which triggered regional fallback and aggressive egress shed behavior. This caused cascading capacity shifts and customer-visible tail latency spikes. This hotpatch introduces two cooperating pieces: a transparent fallback timer in the routing/failover layer and a heartbeat surge mender that smooths ephemeral probe bursts. Design: 1) Transparent fallback timer: adds a per-route ephemeral timer (default 3s) that delays triggering a hard fallback/circuit trip for transient degradations while still recording candidate degraded events. If the degradation persists past the timer, existing fallback logic runs unchanged. The timer is feature-flagged and can be tuned per-tenant. 2) Heartbeat surge mender: a lightweight smoothing stage sitting between health probes and the failover decision engine. It applies a sliding-window median+decay correction to heartbeat latency samples and emits a corrected health score. This reduces sensitivity to 1-5s probe noise without masking real regressions. Changes included: - Routing: route/fallback/timer.go (new) — implements timer lifecycle and tenant override. - Health: probes/surge_mender.go (new) — smoothing algorithm, metrics, and tests. - Config: config/flags.yaml — feature flag and per-tenant defaults. - Telemetry: telemetry/heartbeat_metrics.go — new metrics: heartbeat_mender_adjustments, fallback_timer_skips, fallback_timer_triggers. - Tests: unit tests for timer and mender logic, integration harness extension to simulate probe storms. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to staging and run synthetic probe-storm scenarios (completed). 2) Canary in production traffic: 10% of routing planes for 24h (observed reduction in rollback events by ~68%). 3) Gradual rollout to 50% then 100% over 48h each with automated guardrail checks. Feature flag allows immediate rollback. Backout plan: flip feature flag off; routing will immediately stop using the timer and smoothing stage and fall back to previous behavior. Also revert is a single-service config change, no DB migrations. Observability: added dashboards under "Routing / Fallback" for the new metrics and an alert if fallback_timer_triggers exceeds historical baseline by 3x in a sliding 5m window. Compatibility: fully backwards compatible — the fallback path after the timer is identical to prior logic. Tests: unit (coverage 91% for new modules), integration (probe storm simulations), e2e scripted canary that validated SLO preservation. Security: no secrets or permissions changes. Impact: reduces noisy short-lived cross-region failovers and lowers tail latency during transient network events; small added memory for per-route timer state (~<1MB per plane). Related: SUP-4372 documented customer incident reproduced in test harness. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in ENG-5782 - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Telemetry and dashboards - [x] Feature flag - [x] Canary rollout - [x] Post-merge monitoring on-call runbook Notes: tuned default timer to 3s after testing on three representative customers. Longer defaults delayed legitimate failovers in stress tests; shorter defaults did not sufficiently suppress churn. We allow per-tenant override for edge cases.
commit_summary: Add fallback timer lifecycle and tenant overrides (route/fallback/timer.go)
Implement heartbeat surge mender and tests (probes/surge_mender.go)
discussion: Diego Morales: Could the timer hide real partial outages? Request adding a guard that increments a counter if failures occur while timer active. Aisha: Added fallback_timer_triggers metric and unit that records events when the timer expires — included in telemetry section.

Priya Raman: Suggest lowering default to 2s for small customers. Aisha: We tested 2s and it didn't sufficiently reduce churn for our mid-market cohort; added tenant override and documented tradeoffs in docs/runbooks/fallback_timer.md.

James O'Connor: Please add an e2e assert that ensures requests during a timer window are counted as degraded for SLO reckoning. Aisha: Integration harness updated to mark candidate degraded events and emitted metrics for SLO evaluation.
SRE: Verified canary results in us-east-1 and saw no missed real outages in 72h noisy-wire tests. Approved for merge.
QA: Found a race in timer shutdown when route deleted; fix added in commit 3 (timer goroutine shutdown and waitgroup).
merge_summary: Squash-merged into main after successful canary and CI green. Post-merge: on-call observed reduced regional failovers; no rollbacks required.
post_merge_actions: Add retrospective entry to ENG-5782 thread
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: it delays hard fallback decisions only for very short windows to avoid masking persistent outages. The per-tenant override allows us to tune behavior where customers require more aggressive failover.
